The catalogue of
complaints we love
If yours isn't here, it's still probably ours. And when something needs a scan or a surgeon first, we say so at the assessment and point you right.
Backs & necks
The national anthem of desk work. Most back pain is grumpy, not broken, and grumpy responds beautifully to graded movement.
Sounds like
· Morning stiffness that loosens by lunch
· A twinge that reappears every deadline week
· Sciatica-ish zings down one leg
The usual arc
· Calm the flare, keep you moving
· Build hinge strength you can trust
· A desk setup talk we keep to five minutes
Knees, hips & running
From runner's knee to replaced hips. The answer is almost never 'stop running forever'; it's 'run differently for a while'.
Sounds like
· Pain that arrives at kilometre three, rudely
· Stairs down worse than stairs up
· The post-surgery knee that won't straighten
The usual arc
· Load audit: shoes, volume, sleep, the lot
· Strength blocks with actual numbers
· A return-to-sport date we defend

children.innerHTML: Shoulders & the rest
Frozen shoulders, tennis elbows on people who don't play tennis, ankles that never quite healed. The miscellaneous drawer is our favourite drawer.
Sounds like
· Can't reach the top shelf without a plan
· Clicks with commentary from bystanders
· An old sprain that 'never came right'
The usual arc
· Hands-on relief early, if it earns its keep
· Progressive loading, tracked visit to visit
· Graduation criteria, not endless reviews
House beliefs
Things we'll say out loud
01 — Rest is a dosage, not a lifestyle. We'll prescribe exactly how much.
02 — Scans show shark bites in people who feel fine. We treat you, not your MRI.
03 — If you're not stronger when you leave than when you arrived, we've done half a job.
04 — Discharge is the goal. Clinics that see you forever are called gyms, and gyms are cheaper.
